The '''2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Arkansas''' were held on November 8, 2022, to elect the four [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. representatives]] from the [[U.S. state|state]] of [[Arkansas]], one from each of the state's four [[Arkansas's congressional districts|congressional districts]]. The elections coincided with the [[2022 Arkansas gubernatorial election|Arkansas gubernatorial election]], as well as other elections to the [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections|U.S. House of Representatives]], [[2022 United States Senate elections|elections]] to the [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]], and various [[2022 United States elections|state and local elections]]. Primary elections were held on May 24.

[[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nominee John White attracted attention when, unusually for a member of his party, he denied the legitimacy of President [[Joe Biden]] and the [[2020 United States presidential election]] during a debate.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-10-17 |title=Candidates for Arkansas' 4th Congressional District face off in debate |url=https://www.ualrpublicradio.org/local-regional-news/2022-10-17/candidates-for-arkansas-4th-congressional-district-face-off-in-debate |access-date=2022-11-13 |website=[[KUAR]] |language=en |author=Breen, Daniel}}</ref> White also claimed that "the American people have not legitimately elected a president since [[John F. Kennedy|Kennedy]]." After the debate, the [[Arkansas Democratic Party]] released a statement denouncing White and his claims of election fraud.<ref>{{cite news |work=[[KARK-TV]] |access-date=November 29, 2023 |url=https://www.kark.com/news/your-local-election-hq/arkansas-democrats-distance-party-from-house-candidates-debate-claims-election-denials/ |author1=Kienlen, Alex |date=October 17, 2022 |title=Arkansas Democrats distance party from House candidate's debate claims, election denials |author2=Epperson, Andrew}}</ref>
